description.narrative:
This project will promote an enabling environment for Key, vulnerable and priority Populations to seek and utilise Health <(>&<)> other social service in their respective localities. Using dialogues at community level, key, vulnerable and priority populationswillraise their voices about the issues that affect them and put to a task the duty bearers to find possible remedies that can be used to improve their livelihoods. Enhanced capacity of Key, vulnerable and priority Populations to participate in development interventions, increased community awareness of the causes and effects of poor livelihoods among males and young men and improved reception by health and other social service providers. The project will enhance the institutional capacity of OCE toachieve project goals, objectives, and OCE’s mission.
The negative effects of COVID-19 pandemic has led to high incidences and prevalence of HIV/AIDS <(>&<)> poor livelihoods among these Key, vulnerable and priority populations in Lyantonde. While the HIV prevalence in Uganda has reducedto 5.5%, in Lyantonde district it has remained at 9.5% (Ministry of Health Population based HIV Impact Assessment report 2020) which is unacceptably high. This fact, coupled with poverty, forces males and young men into risky sexual behaviours. They live in denial due to stigma and discrimination from the communities thus deny them their rights to access health and other social services. They do not have the required employable skills hence the project is intended to empowerthem with non-formal skills to help them earn incomes to improve their livelihoods thus reduced exposure to risky sexual and other behaviours. The project will work for increased awareness of the available policies that promote inclusive access to Health<(>&<)> other social services for key, vulnerable and priority populations. It will also work towards improving their socio-economic capacity through skilling to have other alternative sources of incomes

participating-org.narrative:
Organization for Community Empowerment Lyantonde (OCE) is a Non-Governmental Organization (NGO) founded in 2016 by a group of academics, social scientists, and other individuals to respond to the causes and effects of mass poverty, poor livelihoods, diseases likeHIV/AIDS and other pandemics. OCE is registered with NGO bureau of the Ministry of Internal Affairs Kampala and we possess a nationwide operational mandate but currently operates in Lyantonde, Ntungamo and Kabale Districts. Since its inception, OCE’s interventions have been geared towards Health rights promotion for the vulnerable people in society, Promotion of initiatives for the disadvantaged people (Orphans and other vulnerable children People with disabilities, People Living with HIV and AIDS, Key vulnerable <(>&<)> priority populations), Promotion of access to quality Education (formal and non-formal) and Research/Information. These program areas guided our interventions up to 2021. We have however enriched our program areas in the new strategic plan 2022-2027 as follows; I. Promotion of quality health services for the vulnerable people in the Communities. II. Enhancing Community based socio-economic initiatives for vulnerable people. III. Promotion of Quality Education (Formal and Non formal): IV. Promote accessibility to safe water, Sanitation and clean environment. V. Promotion of Gender equity and women empowerment. VI. Strengthening the institutional capacity of OCE to sustainably respond to and implement development interventions.
Since inception in 2016 OCE has made tremendous contribution towards the HIV and AIDS epidemic control. We have made our contributions through projects we have implemented for instance we reached out to 1,771 people with counselling and testing services during the Lyantonde World AIDS day commemoration project 2018.We also reached out to 7679 adolescents with information on HIV and AIDS prevention, sexual reproductive health rights and Life skills with the satisfactory HIV testing counselling and adherence to treatment for men and adolescents in Lyantonde district 2018 - 2020. We supported 1200 students with safe drinking water through installation of water purifying systems in schools 2019. We have mobilised our community members (186 key populations) into savings and loan associations. This has helped them to save and borrow moneyto start income generating activities and have improved their livelihoods. We have promoted inclusion of key populations in accessto social services through promoting the peer approach. We have empowered 110 male champions and peer educators who have since beenattached to health facilities to link out community members into HIV prevention and treatment services.
We have reached out to 756Key populations with HIV prevention and support services under the Cross-border HIV project 2021- 2022.
